blocks.text: The major portion of sulfur, around 85 per cent, is used to produce sulfuric acid. The molecule has a tetrahedral structure with two S-O (hydroxyl) and two S=O bonds (Figure 12.11). The following topics describe its manufacture by the contact process, its physical and chemical properties, and its uses.

blocks.alt: Structural formula of sulfuric acid: a central sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens and two OH groups. Red double arrows give the bond lengths: S=O 142.2 pm, S-O(H) 157.4 pm and O-H 97 pm. A box says the arrangement round sulfur is tetrahedral, sulfur is +6, and about 85% of sulfur is used to make H2SO4.
blocks.caption: Structure of H2SO4 (original diagram after Figure 12.11).

blocks.prompt: Draw the structure of sulfuric acid and give the oxidation state of sulfur in it (exercise Q.2j; MCQ IX).
blocks.explanation: A central sulfur bonded tetrahedrally to four oxygens: two as S=O and two as S-OH. With hydrogen +1 and oxygen -2, 2 + S - 8 = 0, so sulfur is +6.

items: About 85% of sulfur goes into H2SO4; tetrahedral molecule with two S=O and two S-OH bonds; S is +6.
